key_insight: In ceria-based rare-earth high-entropy oxides, oxygen-ion transport is controlled by both vacancy concentration and the local cation network, with best diffusion at moderate vacancy levels and enhanced mobility when Ce-rich pathways are present.
engineering_relevance: These results point to composition and structure tuning as practical levers for designing higher-conductivity solid-state electrolyte ceramics.
method: Classical molecular dynamics with CHGNet machine-learned interatomic potentials
Benchmarked three CHGNet variants against targeted DFT data including f-electrons
Mapped oxygen diffusion versus temperature, Ce fraction, vacancy concentration, and crystal structure
evidence_signal: The study compares multiple ML potential variants to DFT validation data and uses the resulting simulations to extract diffusivity, activation energies, and individual hopping events across compositions and structures.
watch_item: Predictive fidelity depends on the quality of the CHGNet training/transfer to lanthanide-containing oxides, so extrapolation beyond the benchmarked composition space should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Ionic Diffusion Properties of Rare-Earth High-Entropy Oxides from a Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential
